'''Gary Barrett''' (January 3, 1940 – April 10, 2022)<ref>[https://www.ecology.uga.edu/in-memoriam-gary-w-barrett-1942-2022/ In Memorian: Gary W. Barrett, 1942-2022]</ref> was an American ecologist.<ref name="Lidicker1995">{{cite book|last=Lidicker|first=William Zander|title=Landscape approaches in mammalian ecology and conservation|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=933ZQibVgnkC&pg=PA155|accessdate=21 May 2011|year=1995|publisher=U of Minnesota Press|isbn=978-0-8166-2587-1|pages=155–}}</ref>

Barrett held the [[Eugene P. Odum]] chair of [[Odum School of Ecology]] at [[University of Georgia]]; previously he taught at [[Miami University]] and [[Drake University]]. He was the ''Deputy Director for Research'' for the Institute of Environmental Sciences{{Clarify|date=January 2011}} from 1977 to 1981, and was the recipient of the [[US Regional Association of the International Association for Landscape Ecology]]'s Distinguished Landscape Ecologist Award in 2001.{{Citation needed|date=January 2011}}

He received his [[bachelor's degree]] ''[[cum laude]]'' from [[Oakland City University]], his [[Master's degree|master's]] from [[Marquette University]], and his [[doctorate]] from the University of Georgia.
He was one of the founders of Miami University's Institute of Environmental Sciences (IES) in 1969.  IES has conferred Master of Environmental Science degrees for over 50 years.
